title: You Must Enjoy Your Life
why: Single-speaker podcast short that never sits still: a cut every 1.4 s, captions that sit where the speaker is talking into, B-roll and archive stills exactly on the nouns, no dead air. The format Reelsaw clips should converge on.

patterns.name: captions come out of the speaker's mouth
patterns.what: Speaker is framed in the left third, looking right. Captions are placed beside and just below his mouth, in the empty space he faces (caption centre x≈0.65, y≈0.50; mouth at x≈0.33, y≈0.37), so the words read as his speech, not as a subtitle bar. On B-roll and stills the captions keep y≈0.50 and move to x=0.50.

patterns.name: one to three words on screen
patterns.what: Never a sentence. Words appear in speech rhythm, 1-3 at a time; when a noun phrase completes, the phrase stacks into two lines with the noun larger ('in superficial / PURSUITS', 'opposite / PROBLEM', 'this is a big / ISSUE').
patterns.where: 8.5-9 ('temporary / relief'), 10-11 ('in superficial / pursuits'), 14.5-15 ('this is a big / issue'), 18 ('opposite / problem')

patterns.name: emphasis by typeface switch, not only colour
patterns.what: Default is bold white sans. The payoff word switches to an italic script/serif face ('arguing', 'void', 'noticing.', 'seriousness', 'Inverse Law') or to a much larger bold ('TO YOU.', 'CONGRATULATIONS!'). Colour is used sparingly: one gold word per 20-30 s ('the underlying', 'joy').
patterns.where: 7.5 ('arguing'), 12 (gold 'the underlying'), 13 ('existential void'), 18.5 ('Frankl's Inverse Law'), 24 (gold 'joy'), 45 ('TO YOU.'), 69 ('noticing.'), 75 ('from the outside'), 90 ('CONGRATULATIONS!'), 96 ('seriousness')

patterns.name: a cut every 1.4 s, no shot over 8 s
patterns.what: 65 scene changes in 109 s (35.7/min, median shot 1.35 s, longest 8.3 s). Talking head is about 55 % of screen time; it is broken by a cut-away roughly every 4-6 s even when nothing visual is needed.

patterns.name: B-roll on the noun, three kinds
patterns.what: A named person gets their archive photo within a word of the name (Viktor Frankl at 1.3 s, Frankl again at 18.6, Alan Watts at 34.8). An abstract noun gets 1-2 s of stock or film footage that illustrates it (corridor for 'themselves', skate bowl for 'pursuits', crowd on a bridge for 'issue', a runner for 'toward'). A connective phrase that has no image gets a solid-colour card (mint, #40e0c0-ish) with the words alone ('temporary relief', 'THEY WOULDN'T'). Film clips are recognisable movie moments (laughing, crying, running) used as reaction shots.
patterns.where: 1.3 (Frankl photo), 4 (corridor, 'themselves'), 8.5 (colour card 'temporary relief'), 10 (skate bowl, 'pursuits'), 14.5 (bridge crowd, 'issue'), 18.5 (Frankl photo again), 24 (laughing, 'joy'), 33 (marshmallow test), 51 (Alan Watts photo), 63 (colour card 'THEY WOULDN'T'), 87 (runner, 'toward')

patterns.name: flat, loud, no dead air
patterns.what: -15.1 LUFS integrated, loudness range 2.2 LU, zero silences over 0.4 s at -35 dB across 109 s. Every pause is cut; the speech is compressed so cut-aways and jump cuts have no level jumps. Transitions between talking head and B-roll are straight cuts with the voice continuous underneath; no whoosh or hit was audible.

patterns.name: name-drop in the first two seconds
patterns.what: Opens mid-sentence on 'there's a famous Viktor Frankl quote' with the Frankl photo at 1.3 s and the quote card by 2.5 s. No title card, no channel bumper, the first cut-away happens before the viewer can scroll.

patterns.name: off-centre speaker leaves room for the words
patterns.what: The vertical crop puts the speaker's face in the upper-left third rather than centred, so the right half of the frame is free for captions at mouth height and the mic stays in shot. The crop holds still; movement comes from cuts, not from the crop following the face.

gaps.pattern: captions come out of the speaker's mouth
gaps.today: Caption position is a global y with centred x (styleSchema.captionPosition / resolveStyle); nothing ties it to the face box the layout stage already has. A caption anchor mode 'beside the speaker' would place x on the side the face looks into and y at mouth height, falling back to centre on cut-aways.

gaps.pattern: one to three words on screen
gaps.today: maxWords in the style already supports 1-3 words; stacked two-line phrase with larger noun does not exist (captions.ts karaoke renders one event per word at one size).
Emphasis is emphasisColor plus a size bump only (captions.ts); no per-word font switch. RESEARCH.md gap #2.

Cut-aways do not exist; the only motion is the crop track. RESEARCH.md gaps #6 (punch-in zooms) and #12 (B-roll) are the two levers; punch-ins on emphasis words would get the cadence up without any external footage.

No B-roll, no stills, no colour cards. The entities stage already extracts named people; a colour card with the caption alone is the cheapest first step (no external asset) and the library spec gives the asset store for stock. RESEARCH.md gap #12.
No loudness normalisation; silence trimming is on the roadmap (RESEARCH.md gap #3, #10). loudnorm to -15/-16 LUFS plus a silence cut at 0.4 s would match.
Framing centres the face (layout.ts). A 'leave room for captions' rule in the crop (bias toward the side the face looks away from) is a layout change, not a caption change.
